language.script_notes: In the far north-west, indigenous-language place names appear; standard Portuguese signage and BR-XXX shields still apply.

road_furniture.bollard_color: No standard bollard, as elsewhere in Brazil.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Rare — most covered roads are single-carriageway highways through forest with no barrier.
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow centre line and white edge lines on the paved highways (BR-319, BR-364, BR-163); long stretches are unpaved red dirt with no markings at all.
road_furniture.curb_style: Kerbs only in the river cities (Manaus, Belém, Porto Velho).
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The national ladder-and-holes concrete pole in towns. Elsewhere expect dead-straight red-dirt roads cut through rainforest, river ports and vehicle ferries.

architecture.roof_style: Simple gables; deep eaves and verandas against the rain.
architecture.roof_material: Fibre-cement and metal sheeting; some terracotta tile in the cities.
architecture.wall_construction: Timber, including houses raised on stilts (palafitas) along riverbanks that flood seasonally; brick and render in town centres.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Weathered bare timber, whitewash and faded bright paint.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stilt houses over water and mud; wooden riverboats and floating river ports; Manaus's colonial-era centre and opera house.

nature.vegetation: Dense equatorial Amazon rainforest over almost the whole region — a solid green wall along the road — with huge rivers. Tocantins in the south-east is the exception, with drier cerrado savanna.
nature.terrain: Flat lowland Amazon basin; the Guiana Highlands and tepuis rise only in the far north (Roraima).
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid and wet year-round, near the equator; frequent heavy rain and overcast skies. Roadside dirt is strongly red-orange lateritic.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur white plate with a blue 'BRASIL' strip; older grey plates; red commercial plates.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorcycles and river boats do much of the work; comparatively few cars, and many are older.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 and Gen 4 where present.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very sparse — essentially the handful of trans-Amazon highways, the area around Manaus and Belém, and some river towns, with large blank regions between. Mostly white car; some boat and trekker coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Amazonian Peru looks identical — the same rainforest wall, red dirt roads and river towns
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Language — Portuguese vs Spanish. Peru uses different plates and signage; Brazil keeps BR-XXX shields and ladder-and-holes concrete poles.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Southern Colombian Amazon has the same jungle, rivers and sparse coverage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Spanish signage and Colombian plates; Colombia's Amazon coverage is even thinner and its road furniture differs.
The North is unbroken rainforest, big rivers, stilt houses and very thin coverage; the Southeast is hilly, developed, densely covered and full of cities.
